title: Sandbox journey templates: first commit → demo
content:
Summary:
This is a lightweight, repeatable kit for a "first-commit → demo" developer journey inside the sandbox. Goal: give a new integrator (internal or external) a predictable 30–90 minute path from cloning the repo to a shareable demo that exercises the SDK, the hosted API, and minimal telemetry so we can measure success and failure points.

Audience:
- New hires in product/SDKS, solutions engineers, early adopter customers, or internal PMs testing an integration.
- Should be consumable without heavy infra (uses local stub + hosted sandbox tokens).

Assumptions / constraints:
- User has node >= 18 and python 3.10 installed (we include both JS and Py microflows).
- Sandbox token with read-only test model access (token provisioning doc: CONFLUENCE: DEV-ONBOARD-SANDBOX-001).
- Minimal network connectivity; fallbacks for offline local mocks included.

Why this is different: quickstarts are usually "API call → example". This doc strings together rituals (what to run first), checkpoint tests (what to assert), and telemetry probes (what to look for in Console) so engineers can iterate and we can measure the onboarding funnel.

Template contents (what to ship in the repo under /microlabs/first-demo):
1) README-lite.md (1 screen) — one-paragraph intent, 3 commands, expected output.
2) quickstarter.js / quickstarter.py — a single-file runnable demo that:
   - loads a prompt template,
   - calls Redwood SDK to create a streaming chat/generation,
   - prints the token breakdown and round-trip latency,
   - posts a small telemetry event to the sandbox telemetry endpoint.
3) smoke-tests/ folder with 3 tiny tests: tokenization sanity, response-liveness (200 within 2s), and structured-output schema check.
4) lab-guide.md — interactive checklist (below).
5) env.example and local-stub server (docker-compose-lite) for offline.

The Ritual (30–90 minute itinerary) — lab-guide.md excerpt:
- 0–5m: clone + install (npm ci or pip -r reqs). Copy env.example → .env and paste sandbox token.
- 5–15m: run local stub (optional) then run quickstarter. Expect: "Assistant: Hello — here's a 2-line summary" and a printed Latency: ~200ms.
- 15–30m: open Redwood Console (Projects → sandbox-microlabs) and verify the request shows up with model id, tokens, and latency. Capture screenshot.
- 30–45m: run smoke-tests and fix misconfigurations (common: env var name mismatch, API host override).
- 45–60m: tweak prompt template and re-run; verify output stability with our small eval promptset (included).
- 60–90m: prepare a one-slide demo and share a recording (or copy-paste output + Console screenshot).

Checklist for success (pass/fail criteria):
- First-run passes smoke-tests on first or second try.
- A telemetry event appears in Console within 30s and contains: request_id, sdk_version, client_lang, model_variant.
- The demo output includes the expected JSON schema if structured-output path used.
- At least one user (internal or customer) makes a change to prompt template within 90m (signals engagement).

Telemetry probes we add to the quickstarter (minimal):
- event: "sdk.microlab.run" payload: { step: start|success|failure, duration_ms, env: sandbox|local-stub }
- metric: distribution of round-trip latency (ms) per request
- tag: sdk_version and language (js|py)
Notes: telemetry endpoint is opt-in in repo (ENV var MLAB_TELEMETRY=true). Data surface should map to Console microsummary for the microlab.

Developer experience requirements (what we should do as product):
- A short onboarding banner in Console linking to the microlab for sandbox projects.
- Auto-provisioning flow for a read-only sandbox token (backend task, JIRA: ENG-4421).
- Per-lab telemetry dashboard with 3 KPIs: first-run success rate, median latency, edit-to-demo time.

Common failure modes (notes to self):
- Token scoping/permission error: user sees 403; add clearer error & link to token provisioning doc.
- Local stub CORS or port clash on macOS: document an alternate port flag.
- Users accidentally use prod token — include a note and detection that flags tokens with "-prod" prefix in logs and prints a stern warning.

Repo file examples (snippets) — JS quickstarter (pseudo):
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const r = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.SANDBOX_TOKEN, baseUrl: process.env.SANDBOX_HOST });
const start = Date.now();
const res = await r.chat.create({ model: 'sandbox-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize company mission in 2 lines' }], stream: false });
console.log('tokens', res.usage);
console.log('latency', Date.now()-start);
// opt-in telemetry ping
if (process.env.MLAB_TELEMETRY === 'true') fetch(process.env.MLAB_TELEMETRY_URL, { method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ event:'sdk.microlab.run', step:'success' }) });

Lab facilitation notes for SEs / PMs running the workshop:
- Keep pacing: if participant is stuck at install >10m, switch to prerecorded demo and continue with Console checks.
- Encourage live prompt edits; the fastest signal of success is an edit that meaningfully changes the output.
- If network is flaky, pivot to local-stub mode and walk through mocking the same telemetry events.

Open questions / TODOs (quick backlog):
- Should we include an LLM prompt linting step in smoke-tests? (Priya to prototype)
- Add language: go + dotnet microflows? (low priority)
- Decide retention window for microlab telemetry summary in Console (default 7 days).
- UX: inline link in Console to repro steps from last failed run (Ethan exploring feasibility).

References + links:
- CONFLUENCE: DEV-ONBOARD-SANDBOX-001 (token provisioning + stack)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/312 (proto microflow submitted)
- JIRA: ENG-4421 (auto-token provisioning backend ticket)
- Slack thread: #devexp-microlabs (C0123ABC45)

Quick personal notes:
- Keep the README to 3 commands. Nobody reads long docs during a live session.
- Avoid heavy config; prefer env flags.
- Ship the JS first (most SEs prefer it), then Py parity in a follow-up PR.

If this looks good I will:
- cut a small GH branch with microlab files under /microlabs/first-demo,
- open a short PR (assign to Ethan),
- and schedule a 30m trial run with 3 internal volunteer SEs next week.

Unresolved: the exact telemetry schema (Priya to define minimal required fields by 2026-02-01).

---
End of draft. This is a working doc: expect fragments, TODOs, and rough snippets.
